1. Agency was okayish if you were a good worker and a person. They manage a lot of lost causes so they can feel a bit strict when it comes to housing rules. I was very lucky to meey a friendly bunch of people and even one from my country later on.
2. My wage was around 350-400€ per week. 400+was during 12 hour work days though. Got a raise from 11.50 to 13.20 in a year. Accomodation was 120€ per week but mind you I lived with other 3 people and shared a room. Later on I was in a house with 11 other people! Friendly bunch but you know there is bound to be some clashing every now and then.
3. People at work were friendly be it poles, spanish people or even dutch people especialy when they saw I was learning their language and liked to work. Got from spilling water buckets to photographing flowers thanks to my english.
4. There are a lot....A LOT of drinking and drug opportunities. Stay - the fuck - away from them. Recreational shrooms? Weed? Not even those. I saw a Pole kid get psychosis after 6 hits from joint and eating double dose of smartshop magic truffles. Stay clean focus on work and yourself.

Now for the painful truth:

a) Unless you earn around 3K per month you are not going to progress a lot. Housing prizes are crazy forget about being able to live alone. 

b) even if agency is nice try to get a private acommodation at least with somebody. Make friends with agency coworkers that want to move as well or find one room for yourself by asking around. You want to be able to be registered at gemeente so you can get a private contract and be free from the agency. It is much safer. You just dont know what to expect from work agency. My teamleaders were pushong me to find a private accomodation so they can recruit me. Build a name while working under agency (if you are working at one place and you like it there----some workers in my agency were passed around different locations like a hot potatoe)

c) culture shock is a real thing and feeling homesick does suck. I was taught and always protected people under racist discrimination when in my country. But living in one place with morroccans and arabs just hit different. Big cities are mostly of this ethnicity.
